chapter: Day job, war and Bocage's band
title: Bocage's demands on a piano player, his drummers and discipline
summary: Bocage wanted a leading piano style and was strict about tempo, drinking and dress.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Most of that I was over the age. I was 32, you see, when I was in the Southern. Oh, I see. The only thing we had that was very good was what Pete wanted on piano.
What Pete and Charlie Bocas wanted out of a piano.

Yeah. Well it was hard on piano players and drummers, you see, and all. My, I was used to playing mostly stock numbers, you know, orchestrations, and giving the band support, compliments more, you know. And when I joined his band, well he wanted to lead, fill in them, you see. Yeah. He didn't believe in your countenance. Playing chords. No, he didn't believe in playing chords. And the drummers, he was hard on them with the tempos, you know, trying to hold his tempo that he set. He would complain if they speeded up the tempo.
Oh yeah, he called it out. He was hard on them sometimes. He didn't mean a horn, but you know.
Yeah, very strict. And you think he was the only band leader that was at that point, that you played with? That I know of, yeah.
And he was very strict about drinking and things like that too. I see. He had certain times. Of course his band, he never had to worry about that.
Nobody would get drunk. No, no. I mean, pure only strict on that.
